description: Fan out N parallel workers, drain them, and return one report. Use for /swarm, 'swarm this', or parallel coverage, races, gauntlets, and exploration.

sections: Opens a todolist with one entry each for Frame, Fan out, Aggregate and Report.
States the done test, picks slices or a race, fixes the race rule first, and names SHAs and method for measurements.
Spawns all workers in one message, in the cloud by default. Each brief stands alone: goal, scope, check, report format.
Reads final results, respawns once any that skipped the SHAs or method, records a gap after that, applies the race rule.
Returns one in-chat report: a result table, one line per issue, gaps and dropouts, and the race rule used.

lessons.title: Make every brief stand alone
lessons.does: Each helper AI gets the full goal, scope and way to check, so none goes off track for lack of context.
lessons.why: Helpers can't see your chat, so this forces the AI to write the context in instead of assuming it.
lessons.try: When you hand off work, add: "Write it so a new colleague who missed our discussion could act on it."

lessons.quote: A gap does not count as a pass.
lessons.quoteTr: A gap does not count as a pass.
lessons.title: Say what a missing result means
lessons.does: When a helper returns nothing, the report names the gap instead of counting it as passed.
lessons.why: AIs tend to read "no error" as "no problem"; deciding up front what a blank means closes that door.
lessons.try: Add to a checklist: "Pages you didn't check count as failed; list them separately."

lessons.quote: For a race or mixed shape, declare `first pass`, `rank all`, or `best-of` before spawning.
lessons.quoteTr: For a race or mixed shape, declare `first pass`, `rank all`, or `best-of` before spawning.
lessons.title: Set the winning rule first
lessons.does: When several helpers race on one job, how the winner is picked is fixed before they start, so it can't shift afterward.
lessons.why: Rules set before the results stop the AI from picking whichever standard suits the outcome.
lessons.try: Say before starting: "Of the three versions, we keep whichever loads fastest." Then begin.

lessons.title: Ask for all, not the first
lessons.does: It lists every problem it can prove, instead of stopping at the first.
lessons.why: AIs tend to stop at the first find; saying "not only the first" breaks that habit.
lessons.try: For a contract review: "Find every clause that works against me, not just the first one."

blocks: Open a todolist with one entry per phase before launching anything.

1. State the done predicate and the artifact or report the swarm must return.
2. Choose the shape. Partition into slices, race N workers on identical briefs, or mix both. For a race or mixed shape, declare `first pass`, `rank all`, or `best-of` before spawning.
3. Pick the worker model from the `swarm workers` line in the pstack settings file (`~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` in Cursor, `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md` in Claude Code, `~/.agents/pstack-models.md` in other harnesses). If the file or that line is missing, use `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`. For `auto` or `inherit-parent`, omit `model` so the workers run on the parent model. If your subagent tool rejects a slug, use the default and say so. If it rejects the default, use the closest valid slug of the same family from its error message or your harness's model list. For a model race, name each arm's model up front. Pick each subagent's reasoning level for the job, per the Subagents section of the **poteto-mode** skill.
4. Give each worker its own writable output when it writes. When workers verify or measure commits, each brief names the exact SHAs. A measurement brief also names the method (sample count, what one sample is, order). The worker records both in its result.

Spawn all N workers in one message with `subagent_type: generalPurpose`, `environment: "cloud"`, `run_in_background: true`, and the step 3 model, left unset for `auto` or `inherit-parent`. Use `environment: "local"` only when the worker needs access to something on the user's computer.
When a worker must start from a non-default pushed branch, pass `cloud_base_branch`.

**Other harnesses.** These parameters belong to Cursor's `Task` tool, and `environment: "cloud"` runs a Cursor cloud agent. In another harness, use its subagent tool: `Agent` in Claude Code (`subagent_type: general-purpose`), `task` in OpenCode (`subagent_type: general`), `spawn_agent` in Codex. Workers run locally there, so give each one its own worktree or output path. Keep the brief and the model. Drop parameters your tool doesn't have. If your harness has no subagent tool, as in Pi without an extension, run the workers yourself, one after another.

Every brief stands alone. Include the goal, scope, exact slice or race arm, how to verify, and what to report. Reports use `PASS`, `ISSUES`, or `BLOCKED` with evidence. A worker that can prove a defect reports `ISSUES` and lists every issue it can prove, not only the first.
If a worker drops out, proceed with N-1 and note it.

Read the terminal results. Drop a result that does not record the SHAs and method its brief names, and respawn that worker once. After a second miss, record a gap. A gap does not count as a pass. For coverage, every required slice needs a result. For a race, apply the selection rule declared up front. Use first pass, rank all, or best-of. Do not paste raw worker dumps.
Return one consolidated in-chat report with a result table, issue one-liners, gaps or dropouts, and the race rule when used.
